title: Drop the E
kidRule: When a word ends in a silent E, you usually drop the E before adding an ending that starts with a vowel, like ING, ER, EST or Y: arrive becomes arriving. Keep the E when the ending starts with a consonant (homeless), and in a few odd words like canoeing.
hint: Say the small word hiding inside first. It ends with a quiet letter. What happens to that quiet letter when an ending joins on?
reminder: Drop the silent E before you add an ending that starts with a vowel, like I-N-G.

check.question: Why is there no E in ARRIVING?
check.correctAnswer: ARRIVE ends in a silent E, and we drop it before adding ING!
distractors: Because the letter V pushes every E out of a word
Because words with ING are never allowed another vowel

words.sent: The train is arriving at the station right now.
words.story: Arctic terns fly from the top of the world to the bottom and back every year, arriving after a trip of tens of thousands of miles!
words.card: The llama is *arriving* *in* a hot-air balloon!

words.def: Making up your mind about something.
words.sent: I am still deciding which book to read first.
words.story: Honeybees have a clever way of deciding on a new home: scout bees dance for their favorite spot until the swarm agrees!
words.card: The dragon is *deciding* what to have for *din*ner: toast or more toast!

words.def: Moving your body in time to music.
words.sent: Everyone was dancing in the kitchen.
words.story: Honeybees tell each other where the flowers are by dancing a wiggly dance inside the hive!

words.def: Bright and gleaming when light hits it.
words.sent: I found a shiny coin on the sidewalk.
words.story: People say magpies steal shiny things, but when scientists tested it, the birds were actually nervous of them!
words.card: I bumped my *shin* on a *shiny* robot!

words.def: Showing more courage than anyone else.
words.sent: The bravest puppy walked right up to the vacuum cleaner.
words.story: Killdeer birds are some of the bravest parents: they pretend to have a broken wing to lead danger away from their nest!
words.card: The *bravest* mouse wore a tiny *vest* to meet the cat!

words.def: Not what you expected at all.
words.sent: The ending of the story was very surprising.
words.story: Here is a surprising fact: a group of flamingos is called a flamboyance!
words.card: A *surprising* balloon was *rising* out of my cereal bowl!

words.def: So surprising or good that it is hard to believe.
words.sent: The magician did an amazing trick.
words.story: Amazing but true: an octopus has three hearts and blue blood!
words.card: *Zing*! The *amazing* popcorn flew across the room!

words.def: Making you feel thrilled and full of energy.
words.sent: The roller coaster ride was exciting.
words.story: When something exciting happens, your heart beats faster to get your body ready for action!
words.card: The *exciting* parade marched right past a *tin* robot!

words.def: Worth a lot of money, or very important to someone.
words.sent: The museum keeps its most valuable painting behind glass.
words.story: Saffron is the most valuable spice in the world, because each tiny thread has to be picked from a flower by hand!
words.card: The pirate was not *able* to find his most *valuable* sock!

words.def: Making a picture of something in your mind.
words.sent: I keep imagining a castle made of pancakes.
words.story: Albert Einstein did some of his best thinking by imagining what it would be like to ride alongside a beam of light!
words.card: I was *imagining* a whale *in* my bathtub blowing bubbles!
